memes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
memes.statement: A foreign self-employed person who works in Belgium needs a Limosa declaration before the first working day; the client should ask for the L1 receipt.

quotes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
quotes.text: First, the Lima so declaration — it has to be done before the first working day, and you, as the client, should ask for the L1 receipt.

quote.text: Yes, exactly — we had the same with a German freelancer in spring, I checked it on the Limosa portal then.

memes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
memes.statement: An A1 certificate from the home country's social security office shows which country's social security applies to a cross-border freelancer; without it there is a risk of paying contributions in two countries.

quotes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
quotes.text: Second, the a one certificate. He requests it from the Dutch social security office, and it shows that he stays insured in the Netherlands.

quotes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
quotes.text: Without the a one, there is a risk that he has to pay contributions in both countries.

memes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
memes.statement: If a client sets fixed working hours or gives instructions to a freelancer, flag the case to a Senior Expert before the contract is signed, because of the risk of bogus self-employment.

suggested.title: Flag freelancer cases with fixed hours to a Senior Expert

quotes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
quotes.text: that's the schijn zelf standig heid risk, bogus self-employment.

quotes.speaker: senior.expert@sdworx.example
quotes.text: Internally, our rule is: whenever a client sets fixed hours or gives instructions to a freelancer, the case is flagged to a Senior Expert before the contract is signed.

notes: The guest appears as 'Lotte (Guest)' and cannot be mapped to a user; the uploader is asked to resolve it (FR-MT3) and leaves it unmapped.

All statements are generic: no consultant name, client name, rate or dates.
